nodes.description:
The initiating lesion. Reported alleles span splice-site changes, frameshifts, a missense variant, and - most often - whole or partial gene deletions.
The founding DFNB22 allele is the splice variant IVS12+2T>C, found homozygous in a consanguineous Palestinian family. Later series are dominated by copy-number variants, which is a consequence of where the gene sits rather than of any special mutability of its coding sequence.
A third allele class is worth separating out because it is neither a point variant nor a deletion, and neither a sequencing pipeline nor a copy-number pipeline is built to find it: **gene conversion from the OTOAP1 pseudogene**. Pseudogene sequence is copied into the functional gene, carrying a premature stop at p.Glu787* in exon 22. The converted tracts reported span roughly 900 bp to over 9 kbp, and the two probands described were compound heterozygous for a converted allele and a deletion - so the conversion is doing half the work in a genotype that a deletion assay would report as a single heterozygous finding.
Deletions also extend beyond the gene. A homozygous 250 kb deletion at 16p12.2 spanning METTL9, IGSF6 and OTOA segregated with non-syndromic hearing loss in a South Indian consanguineous family, which is worth knowing because a contiguous-gene deletion invites the question of whether the neighbours contribute - and here the phenotype was non-syndromic, so on the available evidence they do not.

nodes.description:
Reserved for the minority whose loss is severe-to-profound. The lesion is upstream of the spiral ganglion, so an implant's target is intact, and no cochlear malformation has been described in this disease.
As with amplification, no DFNB22 implant outcomes are published and none are asserted here.

The functional lesion. Inner hair cell tuning stays sharp - the cells are being driven at the right frequency - but the drive itself is too weak, so compound action potential thresholds rise while masker tuning curves remain narrow. That dissociation is what identifies the defect as one of stimulation rather than of transduction or of frequency selectivity.
A binding caveat. GO:0050910 covers detection of the mechanical stimulus, which includes transduction inside the hair cell, so it is broader than the claim made here: the stimulus never arrives, the cell itself being intact. GO has no term for delivery of a mechanical stimulus to a hair bundle as distinct from its detection, so the narrower reading is carried in preferred_term.

nodes.description:
The mainstay for a sloping mild-to-severe loss, which is what most reported probands have. Amplification is well matched to this disease in principle: the afferent pathway is intact and the deficit is that the inner hair cells are under-driven, so delivering more acoustic energy addresses the actual failure.
No DFNB22-specific outcome data exist. Recorded without an evidence item rather than with a quote from the general amplification literature, which would not be about this disease.

Otoancorin is GPI-anchored to the apical surface of non-sensory epithelial cells and is restricted to the zones where those surfaces contact an acellular gel. In the cochlea that means the permanent attachment along the top of the spiral limbus, and a transient one over the developing greater epithelial ridge.
The GPI anchorage is not an inference from sequence. It was tested directly: wild-type otoancorin is released from the cell surface by phosphatidylinositol-specific phospholipase C, whereas a truncating variant is shed into the medium uncontrolled. So a C-terminal truncation does not merely shorten the protein, it stops it being held at the surface at all.

nodes.description:
Not a pathological step. It is recorded because it is the part of the cochlea this disease spares, and because sparing it has a clinical consequence: otoacoustic emissions, which report outer hair cell function, can be present in an ear that is nonetheless substantially deaf.
The entry stops short of claiming that OAEs are preserved in DFNB22 patients. The only human measurement on record is a failed newborn screen in one confirmed proband, curated below as REFUTE, and a pass/fail neonatal screen cannot settle what a distortion-product study would. What is asserted in humans is only that the mechanism predicts preserved emissions, and the HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH discussion says so.

nodes.description: The specific structural lesion, and the reason this disease behaves unlike other tectorial membrane disorders. The membrane is not absent, malformed, or displaced away from the organ of Corti. It keeps its ribbon shape and stays in contact with the outer hair cells. Only its inner edge, where it should be moored to the limbus, comes free.
